name: Sentry
look: Two-polarity canvas — violet midnight for marketing, white for reference — with a lime keyword highlight used as a typographic device.

hero.title: Code breaks. Fix it faster.
hero.sub: Errors with the stack trace, the release, the commit and the user session attached — so triage is reading rather than reconstructing.

features.title: Context, not just a count
features.sub: An error is only useful with the release, the commit, the environment and the session that produced it.

items.title: Error monitoring
items.body: Grouped by root cause rather than by message, with the stack trace mapped back to your source.

items.title: Suspect commits
items.body: The commit most likely to have caused it, identified from the stack frames and blame data.

items.title: Performance
items.body: Slow transactions traced end to end, from the browser through to the query.

items.title: Session replay
items.body: Watch what the user did in the thirty seconds before it broke.

items.title: Alerts that behave
items.body: Route by ownership, escalate on volume, and stay quiet for known noise.

items.title: 100+ platforms
items.body: Every major language and framework, with the SDK doing the context gathering.

showcases.title: The commit, not just the line
showcases.body: When an error appears, the release that introduced it and the commit most likely responsible are already attached. Triage becomes reading a page rather than bisecting a deploy history at midnight.

showcases.title: Quiet by default, loud when it matters
showcases.body: Alert fatigue kills monitoring tools. Issues are grouped by root cause, known noise is suppressed, and escalation is driven by volume and user impact rather than by every individual event.
points: Grouped by root cause, not message

gallery.title: DOCUMENTATION
gallery.sub: SDK setup, source maps, alerting and performance.

testimonial.quote: It told us which commit broke it before anyone had opened the repository. We fixed a production error in eleven minutes on a Sunday, which used to be a whole afternoon.
testimonial.name: Jamie Okoro

pricing.title: PRICING
pricing.sub: A free tier that is genuinely usable, then priced per event.

items.a: By root cause using the stack trace, not by message text. A single bug producing twenty different messages stays one issue rather than twenty.
Grouping, suppression of known noise and impact-based escalation are the defaults. You can also mute an issue permanently rather than repeatedly dismissing it.
Yes, all of them, on GitHub with public issue trackers. The server is source-available and self-hostable.

items.q: Does session replay capture sensitive data?
items.a: Text and inputs are masked by default. You opt in to unmasking specific elements rather than opting out of capturing everything.

cta.title: Stop reconstructing bugs
cta.sub: Free to start, five thousand errors a month, no card.

notes: Two polarities that never blur: violet midnight for marketing and product pages, white for pricing and dense reference content.
The lime highlight is a typographic device, not a swatch — it wraps single words inside a headline like syntax highlighting.
Sticker illustrations appear at section junctions and never inside cards. They create rhythm between dense blocks.
Uppercase eyebrows and button caps with a slight tracking lift give the system its developer-console cadence.
Card chrome follows the canvas: dark sections nest dark cards, light sections nest white ones. Only the polarity flips.
